title: MagicBeanStalk: Escaping the RLVR Zero Advantage Trap with Recursive Data Synthesis
abstract: arXiv:2610.12659v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Data-centric scaling of RLVR has focused on collecting or generating verifiable training problems. However, corpus size alone does not determine whether the dataset provides a useful learning signal for a target policy. To guide the synthesis of effective RLVR data, we experimentally characterize dataset effectiveness as a function of its problems, the target policy, and the training rollout budget. Under this characterization, we show that a large open-source math corpus pooled from widely used RLVR datasets falls almost entirely into a zero-advantage trap: for a fixed target policy and rollout budget, roughly 88% of its problems are solved in every rollout or failed in every rollout. Filtering concentrates what remains, but it can only select, discarding the hard problems. translated_title: MagicBeanStalk：通过递归数据合成摆脱RLVR零优势陷阱
translated_abstract: 以数据为中心的RLVR扩展一直聚焦于收集或生成可验证的训练问题。然而，语料库的规模本身并不能决定该数据集能否为目标策略提供有用的学习信号。为了指导有效的RLVR数据合成，我们通过实验将数据集的有效性刻画为其问题、目标策略和训练rollout预算的函数。在这一刻画下，我们展示了一个汇集自广泛使用的RLVR数据集的大型开源数学语料库几乎完全陷入了零优势陷阱：在固定的目标策略和rollout预算下，大约88%的问题要么在每次rollout中都被解决，要么在每次rollout中都失败。过滤可以浓缩剩余部分，但它只能进行选择，从而丢弃了难题。因此，有效的合成问题应当需要解决那些难题所必需的推理操作及其组合，但其难度必须加以控制（原文在此处截断）。
tldr: 该论文发现主流RLVR数学语料库中约88%的问题因过于简单或过难而无法为目标策略提供有效学习信号（即零优势陷阱），并提出MagicBeanStalk方法，通过递归数据合成生成既蕴含难题所需推理操作、又难度适中的有效训练问题。
en_tdlr: This paper reveals that roughly 88% of problems in mainstream RLVR math corpora fall into a zero-advantage trap—either always solved or always failed—offering no learning signal, and proposes MagicBeanStalk, a recursive data synthesis method that generates effective training problems requiring the reasoning operations of hard ones while keeping their difficulty appropriately calibrated.
